transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this pre-filing review. As you know, we have a non-final office action response due on our automated diagnostic platform patent application in 28 days. The current draft response continues pursuing the existing claim set without filing a continuation. Before I approve the final prosecution plan, I need each of your groups — patent prosecution, product, government contracts, and IP operations — to report any issues that could affect this filing. Let's go around the table.

transcript.text: I need to disclose a critical issue. After the response draft went to internal review, I completed a supplemental prior-art comparison showing that claims 1 through 6 are anticipated by prior art. Claim 7 remains patentable, but only if we narrow the prosecution track to claim 7 alone. I have not yet circulated this comparison because I completed it after the draft was already in review. This directly affects our filing strategy — proceeding with the current draft response pursuing the full existing claim set would likely result in those claims being rejected, and we should consider amending the response to focus on claim 7.

The engineering team needs a continuation focused on the claim 12 improvement. This product requirement was recorded in a launch-planning file rather than the patent matter, which is why it hasn't surfaced in this review until now. transcript.text: I need to raise an IP operations issue. In reviewing the executed inventor records, I found that one inventor's assignment omits the continuation rights needed for this patent family. Before filing any continuation, the company must obtain and record a corrected assignment. I had not raised this earlier because the assignment repository is maintained separately from our docketing system. This directly affects our filing strategy — if we decide to file a continuation, we cannot do so until the corrected assignment is obtained and recorded.
